intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia-51 (SPG51) is caused by homozygous deletion involving the AP4E1 gene (607244) on chromosome 15q21.2.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia-51 (SPG51) is caused by homozygous deletion involving the AP4E1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: This report describes an autosomal recessive form of spastic tetraplegic cerebral palsy with profound intellectual disability, microcephaly, epilepsy and white matter loss in a consanguineous family resulting from a homozygous deletion involving AP4E1
checks.explanation: The paper links the disorder to a homozygous deletion involving AP4E1, but it calls the disorder cerebral palsy or 'AP-4 deficiency syndrome'. The name SPG51 does not appear in the paper.

checks.claim: The AP4E1 gene is located on chromosome 15q21.2.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified a 139 kb (minimum) to 222 kb (maximum) homozygous deletion of chromosome 15q21.2 that includes the 5′ end of two genes: AP4E1 (adaptor related protein complex-4, epsilon-1) and SPPL2A
checks.explanation: The deletion containing AP4E1 is at 15q21.2.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia-51 is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder. It begins with neonatal or infantile hypotonia that progresses to spasticity of the limbs, often spastic tetraplegia, and is accompanied by severe intellectual disability, poor or absent speech, microcephaly and seizures (Moreno-De-Luca et al., 2011). Mild facial dysmorphism has also been reported (Kong et al., 2013). The disorder belongs to the group of disorders caused by deficiency of the adaptor protein complex-4 (AP-4), which Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) called 'AP-4 deficiency syndrome.' Defects in the other AP-4 subunits, AP4B1, AP4M1 and AP4S1, cause clinically similar disorders (Abou Jamra et al., 2011).

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia-51 is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Cerebral palsy is a heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental brain disorders resulting in motor and posture impairments
checks.explanation: The paper describes the disorder as a severe neurodevelopmental cerebral palsy syndrome with profound intellectual disability.

checks.claim: SPG51 begins with neonatal or infantile hypotonia that progresses to spasticity of the limbs.
checks.evidence_quote: At birth she presented with microcephaly and hypotonia that progressed to spastic tetraplegia with hyperreflexia and generalised hypertonia by the first year of life.
checks.explanation: Hypotonia at birth or in infancy progresses to spasticity.

checks.claim: Limb spasticity in SPG51 often takes the form of spastic tetraplegia.
checks.evidence_quote: an autosomal recessive form of spastic tetraplegic cerebral palsy
checks.explanation: The paper reports spastic tetraplegia.

checks.claim: SPG51 is accompanied by severe intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: spastic tetraplegic cerebral palsy with profound intellectual disability, microcephaly, epilepsy and white matter loss
checks.explanation: Severe or profound intellectual disability is reported.

checks.claim: SPG51 is accompanied by poor or absent speech.
checks.evidence_quote: He acquired some dysarthric words, but never normal speech
checks.explanation: One sib had no speech and the other had only a few dysarthric words.

checks.claim: SPG51 is accompanied by microcephaly.
checks.evidence_quote: spastic tetraplegic cerebral palsy with profound intellectual disability, microcephaly, epilepsy and white matter loss
checks.explanation: Microcephaly is reported.

checks.claim: SPG51 is accompanied by seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: Seizures started with staring spells and developed into generalised tonic-clonic at age 15.
checks.explanation: Both sibs had seizures.

checks.claim: Mild facial dysmorphism has been reported in SPG51.
checks.evidence_quote: Both patients presented discreet but remarkable facial gestalt with a prominent, bulbous nose, a wide mouth and coarse features.
checks.explanation: The twins with the AP4E1 mutation had subtle ("discreet") facial dysmorphic features, which matches mild facial dysmorphism.

checks.claim: SPG51 belongs to the group of disorders caused by deficiency of the adaptor protein complex-4 (AP-4).
checks.evidence_quote: disruption of any one of the four subunits of AP-4 causes dysfunction of the entire complex, leading to a distinct 'AP-4 deficiency syndrome'.
checks.explanation: The disorder is attributed to AP-4 deficiency.

checks.claim: Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) called the AP-4 deficiency disorders 'AP-4 deficiency syndrome.'
checks.evidence_quote: causes a distinct autosomal recessive disorder that we refer to as ‘AP-4 deficiency syndrome’.
checks.explanation: The authors coined the term 'AP-4 deficiency syndrome'.

checks.claim: Defects in the other AP-4 subunits, AP4B1, AP4M1 and AP4S1, cause disorders clinically similar to SPG51.
checks.evidence_quote: we identified one mutation in each of three genes encoding adaptor protein complex 4 (AP4) subunits: a nonsense mutation in AP4S1 (NM_007077.3: c.124C>T, p.Arg42(∗)), a frameshift mutation in AP4B1
checks.explanation: The paper reports AP4S1 and AP4B1 (and AP4E1) mutations in its patients, who share one clinically recognizable AP4-deficiency syndrome. AP4M1 is mentioned only as previously reported work (cerebral palsy with severe intellectual disability). The paper does not itself show that AP4M1 defects cause a similar disorder.

paragraphs.text: Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) described a consanguineous family in which 2 sibs had a condition described as cerebral palsy. Both had spastic quadriplegia, microcephaly, severe intellectual disability and seizures.

checks.claim: Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) described a consanguineous family in which 2 sibs had a condition described as cerebral palsy.
checks.evidence_quote: We evaluated a Palestinian–Jordanian consanguineous family with two siblings affected by an idiopathic neurological condition described as cerebral palsy
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Both affected sibs in the consanguineous family of Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) had spastic quadriplegia.
checks.evidence_quote: On examination at 22 years, he had spastic tetraplegia with hypertonia and hyperreflexia
checks.explanation: Both sibs had spastic tetraplegia, which is the same as spastic quadriplegia (table 1 shows + for both).

checks.claim: Both affected sibs in the consanguineous family of Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) had microcephaly.
checks.evidence_quote: Postnatally he presented with microcephaly and hypotonia
checks.explanation: Both sibs had microcephaly (-3 SD each in table 1).

checks.claim: Both affected sibs in the consanguineous family of Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) had severe intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: Severe cognitive deficits were noted, as well as adaptive impairments, with all age equivalents <1 year of age.
checks.explanation: Both sibs had severe or profound intellectual disability.

checks.claim: Both affected sibs in the consanguineous family of Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) had seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: has been wheelchair-bound since 5 years of age, when she also started experiencing generalised tonic-clonic seizures.
checks.explanation: Both sibs had seizures (epilepsy + for both in table 1).

paragraphs.text: Abou Jamra et al. (2011) reported consanguineous families with AP-4 deficiency, including a family with an AP4E1 mutation. Affected individuals had severe intellectual disability, absent speech, early hypotonia that progressed to spastic paraplegia, and short stature. Some also had microcephaly.

checks.claim: Abou Jamra et al. (2011) reported consanguineous families with AP-4 deficiency, including a family with an AP4E1 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: eight affected individuals who were from three consanguineous families
checks.explanation: The abstract describes three consanguineous families, one of which carries the AP4E1 splice mutation.

checks.claim: Affected individuals with AP-4 deficiency reported by Abou Jamra et al. (2011) had severe intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: presented with severe intellectual disability, absent speech, shy character
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Affected individuals with AP-4 deficiency reported by Abou Jamra et al. (2011) had absent speech.
checks.evidence_quote: presented with severe intellectual disability, absent speech, shy character
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Affected individuals with AP-4 deficiency reported by Abou Jamra et al. (2011) had early hypotonia that progressed to spastic paraplegia.
checks.evidence_quote: muscular hypotonia that progressed to spastic paraplegia
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Affected individuals with AP-4 deficiency reported by Abou Jamra et al. (2011) had short stature.
checks.evidence_quote: progressive spastic paraplegia, shy character, and short stature
checks.explanation: Short stature appears in the title, and the abstract lists growth retardation.

checks.claim: Some affected individuals with AP-4 deficiency reported by Abou Jamra et al. (2011) had microcephaly.
checks.evidence_quote: muscular hypotonia that progressed to spastic paraplegia, microcephaly, foot deformity
checks.explanation: Microcephaly is listed among the patients' features as a group. The abstract does not say whether only some or all of the patients had it.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of SPG51 in the families reported by Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) and Abou Jamra et al. (2011) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of SPG51 in the family reported by Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: This report describes an autosomal recessive form of spastic tetraplegic cerebral palsy
checks.explanation: The family shows autosomal recessive inheritance: a homozygous deletion in the affected sibs and carrier parents.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of SPG51 in the families reported by Abou Jamra et al. (2011) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Adaptor protein complex 4 deficiency causes severe autosomal-recessive intellectual disability
checks.explanation: The title and abstract describe autosomal recessive inheritance in consanguineous families.

paragraphs.text: Kong et al. (2013) noted that clinically similar autosomal recessive spastic paraplegias are caused by mutation in the genes encoding the other subunits of the AP-4 complex: AP4B1 (SPG47), AP4M1 (SPG50) and AP4S1 (SPG52).

checks.claim: Kong et al. (2013) noted that clinically similar autosomal recessive spastic paraplegias are caused by mutation in genes encoding the other subunits of the AP-4 complex.
checks.evidence_quote: In total, 27 patients from nine kindreds, including nine with AP4E1 mutations, nine with AP4B1 mutations, six with AP4S1 mutations, and three with AP4M1 mutations [4], [5], [6], [7], [8], have a uniform clinical phenotype of type I complex HSP
checks.explanation: The paper says mutations in all four AP-4 subunit genes cause autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia with a uniform phenotype. It also states that 'mutations of the four genes encoding the subunits of the AP-4 (adaptor protein-4) complex have recently been identified in patients with autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia.'

checks.claim: Mutation in AP4B1 causes SPG47.
checks.evidence_quote: AP4B1, SPG47 (OMIM*614066); AP4M1, SPG50 (OMIM*612936); AP4E1 SPG51 (OMIM*613744) and AP4S1, SPG52 (OMIM*614067)
checks.explanation: The paper pairs AP4B1 with SPG47.

checks.claim: Mutation in AP4M1 causes SPG50.
checks.evidence_quote: AP4B1, SPG47 (OMIM*614066); AP4M1, SPG50 (OMIM*612936); AP4E1 SPG51 (OMIM*613744) and AP4S1, SPG52 (OMIM*614067)
checks.explanation: The paper pairs AP4M1 with SPG50.

checks.claim: Mutation in AP4S1 causes SPG52.
checks.evidence_quote: AP4B1, SPG47 (OMIM*614066); AP4M1, SPG50 (OMIM*612936); AP4E1 SPG51 (OMIM*613744) and AP4S1, SPG52 (OMIM*614067)
checks.explanation: The paper pairs AP4S1 with SPG52.

paragraphs.text: In 2 sibs from a consanguineous family with spastic quadriplegic cerebral palsy, Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) identified a homozygous deletion of chromosome 15q21.2 that included the 5-prime end of 2 genes, AP4E1 and SPPL2A. The deletion segregated with the disorder in the family.

checks.claim: Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) studied 2 sibs from a consanguineous family with spastic quadriplegic cerebral palsy.
checks.evidence_quote: We evaluated a Palestinian–Jordanian consanguineous family with two siblings affected by an idiopathic neurological condition described as cerebral palsy
checks.explanation: Two sibs from a consanguineous family with spastic tetraplegic cerebral palsy.

checks.claim: Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) identified a homozygous deletion of chromosome 15q21.2 in the 2 affected sibs.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified a 139 kb (minimum) to 222 kb (maximum) homozygous deletion of chromosome 15q21.2
checks.explanation: Both probands carry the homozygous deletion.

checks.claim: The 15q21.2 deletion identified by Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) included the 5-prime end of the AP4E1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: homozygous deletion of chromosome 15q21.2 that includes the 5′ end of two genes: AP4E1 (adaptor related protein complex-4, epsilon-1) and SPPL2A
checks.explanation: The deletion includes the 5′ end of AP4E1.

checks.claim: The 15q21.2 deletion identified by Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) included the 5-prime end of the SPPL2A gene.
checks.evidence_quote: homozygous deletion of chromosome 15q21.2 that includes the 5′ end of two genes: AP4E1 (adaptor related protein complex-4, epsilon-1) and SPPL2A (signal peptide peptidase-like-2A)
checks.explanation: The deletion includes the 5′ end of SPPL2A.

checks.claim: The 15q21.2 deletion identified by Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) segregated with the disorder in the family.
checks.evidence_quote: Top panel, normal FISH results from the younger sibling (IV-6); middle panel, heterozygous deletion identified in the mother and older sister (III-2, IV-3); bottom panel, homozygous deletion found in both probands (IV-4, IV-5).
checks.explanation: The deletion is homozygous only in the affected sibs. The mother and the older sister are heterozygous, and the younger sibling does not carry it. The father is inferred to be a carrier.

paragraphs.text: Abou Jamra et al. (2011) studied consanguineous families with intellectual disability and spastic paraplegia. In one family they identified a splice mutation in the AP4E1 gene (c.542+1_542+4delGTAA) that resulted in a frameshift and truncation (Glu181GlyfsTer20). In other families of the same study they found mutations in other AP-4 subunit genes.

checks.claim: Abou Jamra et al. (2011) studied consanguineous families with intellectual disability and spastic paraplegia.
checks.evidence_quote: three consanguineous families and presented with severe intellectual disability, absent speech, shy character, stereotypic laughter, muscular hypotonia that progressed to spastic paraplegia
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Abou Jamra et al. (2011) identified a splice mutation in the AP4E1 gene, c.542+1_542+4delGTAA, in one family.
checks.evidence_quote: a splice mutation in AP4E1 (NM_007347.3: c.542+1_542+4delGTAA, r.421_542del, p.Glu181Glyfs(∗)20)
checks.explanation: The variant matches exactly; each of the three families carried a mutation in one gene.

checks.claim: The AP4E1 splice mutation c.542+1_542+4delGTAA resulted in a frameshift and truncation (Glu181GlyfsTer20).
checks.evidence_quote: a splice mutation in AP4E1 (NM_007347.3: c.542+1_542+4delGTAA, r.421_542del, p.Glu181Glyfs(∗)20)
checks.explanation: p.Glu181Glyfs*20 is a frameshift ending in a premature stop codon, which means truncation.

checks.claim: In other families of the Abou Jamra et al. (2011) study, mutations were found in other AP-4 subunit genes.
checks.evidence_quote: we identified one mutation in each of three genes encoding adaptor protein complex 4 (AP4) subunits: a nonsense mutation in AP4S1
checks.explanation: The other two families had mutations in AP4S1 and AP4B1.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Progressive spasticity of the lower limbs
